summary: Right-handed volleyball spike at ball contact: airborne, straight hitting arm high in front of the hitting shoulder.

roles.l_arm: non-hitting arm, pulled down to the chest

environment.text: Net: top tape 2.43 m high, {fwd:net_top:pelvis} cm in front of the hips; ball contact {up:ball:net_top} cm above the tape, on the hitter's own side ({fwd:net_top:ball} cm short of the net plane).

cameras.name: low_three_quarter
cameras.text: Sharp focus on the hitting hand and ball, shallow depth of field, background crowd soft.

cameras.name: across_net
cameras.text: Blocker's point of view from across the net, net tape crossing the lower frame.

cameras.name: wide_side
cameras.text: Cinematic 21:9-style wide frame, athlete at the right third, arena lights behind.

rules.why: straight arm at contact (FIVB: contact with a straight arm; elbow about 14 deg flexion)
shoulder abduction about 130 deg at contact
ball in front of the hitting shoulder
contact at near-full reach above the shoulder
trunk tilts away from the hitting arm to raise the hitting shoulder
airborne at contact; elite male jump height about 0.62-0.64 m

text.action: a volleyball attacker at the peak of a jump spike, striking the ball with a straight right arm high in front of the right shoulder
text.core: Airborne body with both feet {lowest_z} m above the floor and toes pointing down, knees bent; trunk tilted left so the hitting shoulder is higher than the other; right arm almost fully straight overhead, palm on the upper back of the ball; left arm pulled down across the chest; eyes on the ball.
text.gaze: Eyes locked on the ball at the moment of contact.
text.r_arm: Heel of the hand and all five fingers on the upper back half of the ball, wrist starting to snap over it.
text.l_arm: Non-hitting arm has swung down and is tucked close to the chest to speed up trunk rotation.
cues: hitting shoulder, hip and ball form one line
contact the ball at full reach in front of the hitting shoulder
non-hitting arm pulls down as the hitting arm swings through
objects: Ball slightly flattened against the palm; one ball only.
kinetic: motion blur on the hitting forearm and hand along the downward swing path
ball compressing against the palm, spin blur on the ball panels
jersey and hair lifted by the upward jump, sweat droplets flying off the arm
floor far below the feet, shadow on the court under the athlete
avoid: body touching or passing through the net
